original_visible_content.stem: Which covered Massachusetts outpatient dispensings belong in the MassPAT submission stream on the basis of the listed drug? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Gabapentin prescribed for postherpetic neuralgia
Pregabalin prescribed for neuropathic pain
Pseudoephedrine sold in an ordinary CMEA retail transaction
None of the listed transactions

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts MassPAT reporting covers Schedule II through V dispensing and designated additional drugs. Pregabalin is Schedule V, and gabapentin is the designated Massachusetts Schedule VI additional drug in this fixture.

choice_analysis.A: Gabapentin is federally noncontrolled but specifically reportable to MassPAT as a Massachusetts additional drug.
choice_analysis.B: Pregabalin is Schedule V, so a covered outpatient dispensing is included in the reporting stream.
choice_analysis.C: CMEA retail controls do not by themselves convert an ordinary pseudoephedrine sale into a MassPAT dispensing record.
choice_analysis.D: This is incorrect because both gabapentin and pregabalin are reportable on the stated facts.

related_facts: Gabapentin reportability does not change its federal controlled status.
The current dispenser standard generally uses a 24-hour or next-business-day submission framework.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating MassPAT reporting status as if it were a federal schedule.

original_visible_content.stem: During a pharmacy-system configuration audit, the pharmacist reviews rules that would automatically control dispensing or monitoring. Which configurations are legally correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Treat pregabalin as Schedule V and submit covered dispensing to MassPAT.
Treat gabapentin as federally noncontrolled but Massachusetts Schedule VI and MassPAT-reportable.
Treat methylphenidate as Schedule II and block prescription refills.
Apply CMEA retail-sale controls to pseudoephedrine without classifying it as Schedule V solely because of those controls.
Apply the federal Schedule III-IV five-refill/six-month rule to gabapentin solely because Massachusetts places it in Schedule VI.

explanation.core_reasoning: A pharmacy system must keep federal schedule, Massachusetts schedule, MassPAT reporting, refill limits, and CMEA retail controls separate. Pregabalin, gabapentin, and methylphenidate require the stated schedule/PMP/refill configurations, while pseudoephedrine requires its separate CMEA retail controls without being converted into Schedule V. Massachusetts Schedule VI status also does not import the federal Schedule III-IV refill rule into gabapentin.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Pregabalin is Schedule V, and covered Massachusetts dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. Gabapentin is not federally scheduled, but Massachusetts treats it as Schedule VI and includes it in PMP reporting.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Methylphenidate is Schedule II, for which refills are prohibited.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. CMEA imposes separate retail-sale controls on pseudoephedrine without making the product Schedule V solely because of those controls.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. Massachusetts Schedule VI classification does not by itself trigger the federal Schedule III-IV refill ceiling.

related_facts: Monitoring status and controlled-substance schedule are separate legal concepts.
A state scheduling rule does not automatically change a drug's federal schedule.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not convert every monitored or behind-the-counter product into a federally scheduled drug or import federal refill rules from an unrelated schedule.

original_visible_content.stem: At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?

choices.text: Dispense because a stimulant prescription remains valid for six months.
Treat the Schedule II prescription as expired under the 30-day Massachusetts validity rule.
Call the prescriber and use that confirmation to restart the 30-day clock.
Transfer the unfilled prescription so the receiving pharmacy can treat it as new.
Apply the one-year Schedule VI transfer period.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Treat the Schedule II prescription as expired under the 30-day Massachusetts validity rule.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Dispense because a stimulant prescription remains valid for six months.' would require that the prescription were Schedule III or IV and still within the federal refill window. The decisive cue appears in 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Dispense because a stimulant prescription remains valid for six months.' would apply only if the prescription were Schedule III or IV and still within the federal refill window; 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Treat the Schedule II prescription as expired under the 30-day Massachusetts validity rule.': supported by schedule ii validity.
choice_analysis.C: 'Call the prescriber and use that confirmation to restart the 30-day clock.' would apply only if a new prescription bearing a new lawful issue date were issued; 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Transfer the unfilled prescription so the receiving pharmacy can treat it as new.' would apply only if transfer changed neither the original issue date nor Massachusetts validity; 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Apply the one-year Schedule VI transfer period.' would apply only if the drug were Massachusetts Schedule VI rather than Schedule II; 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?' states otherwise.

related_facts: lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) is used for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and moderate to severe binge eating disorder; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.
explanation.mpje_trap: 'Dispense because a stimulant prescription remains valid for six months.' would apply if the prescription were Schedule III or IV and still within the federal refill window. In 'At prescription intake, a Vyvanse prescription is presented 31 days after its issue date with no prior dispensing. What should the Massachusetts pharmacist conclude?', that predicate is missing.

choices.text: Omit it because only Schedule II drugs are reported.

Let the product program replace the PMP submission.
Wait to report unless a refill is later authorized.

explanation.core_reasoning: The stated transaction is a patient-specific Schedule III dispensing by the pharmacy, so the general MassPAT reporting rule applies. Later administration at the clinic does not recharacterize the pharmacy's recorded dispensing.

choice_analysis.A: MassPAT reporting is not limited to Schedule II drugs.
choice_analysis.B: The stem expressly identifies a pharmacy dispensing, distinct from the clinic's later administration.
choice_analysis.C: A product distribution program does not replace a required state PMP submission.
choice_analysis.D: Reporting follows the dispensing transaction, not the existence of a later refill.
choice_analysis.E: Correct. The pharmacy reports the covered Schedule III dispensing.

related_facts: Sublocade is a Schedule III extended-release buprenorphine injection for OUD treatment.

choice_analysis.B: Cash payment is not a reporting exemption.
choice_analysis.C: MassPAT coverage is not limited to opioids.
choice_analysis.D: The general reporting trigger does not depend on a seven-day quantity threshold.

choice_analysis.B: Suvorexant remains Schedule IV despite its insomnia indication.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Schedule IV status brings the covered dispensing within the reporting rule.
choice_analysis.D: Reporting occurs for each covered dispensing, not only after a refill threshold.
choice_analysis.E: Prescriber preference does not control pharmacy PMP reporting.

Covered Massachusetts pharmacy dispensings of Schedule II through V drugs are reportable to MassPAT.

original_visible_content.stem: An adult patient's first outpatient tramadol prescription for acute pain requests a 10-day supply and contains no facts supporting a statutory exception. A technician argues that the Massachusetts seven-day opiate rule cannot apply because tramadol is Schedule IV rather than Schedule II. Which conclusion is most accurate?

choices.text: The technician is correct because the seven-day statute applies only to Schedule II narcotic prescriptions.
The technician is correct because Massachusetts excludes every Schedule IV drug from opiate supply limits.
The prescription is exempt whenever the patient pays cash.
The pharmacy may ignore the supply issue if MassPAT was checked.
The technician is incorrect; Schedule IV status does not exempt tramadol from the separate seven-day opiate rule.

explanation.core_reasoning: The Massachusetts seven-day statute is triggered by an opiate prescription and its patient/use circumstances, not by a requirement that the drug be Schedule II. Tramadol's Schedule IV status therefore does not by itself remove the adult first-outpatient seven-day rule.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. The statute is not written as a Schedule-II-only limit.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Tramadol's Schedule IV classification does not decide whether the opiate supply-limit statute applies.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. Payment method is not the statutory trigger.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. PMP review does not replace compliance with a separate supply-limit statute.
choice_analysis.E: Correct. Apply schedule consequences and opiate supply limits as separate legal dimensions.

related_facts: A qualifying documented exception under § 19D(b) can permit a quantity greater than seven days.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not assume that every opioid-related supply rule is limited to Schedule II drugs.

The pharmacy must satisfy the current Mifepristone REMS pharmacy-certification requirements before dispensing under this pathway.
The prescription must come from a prescriber who satisfies the current Mifepristone REMS prescriber-certification requirement.
Massachusetts Schedule VI status does not erase the separate federal product-specific REMS conditions.
The pharmacy can substitute ordinary Schedule VI transfer documentation for REMS certification because mifepristone is not federally controlled.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacist must apply both the ordinary Massachusetts prescription framework and the product-specific federal REMS. Retail dispensing is possible, but only through the current certified-pharmacy/certified-prescriber pathway.

choice_analysis.A: Current FDA rules allow retail pharmacy dispensing when the pharmacy satisfies the REMS certification requirements.
choice_analysis.B: Pharmacy certification is a current REMS condition for pharmacy dispensing of the drug for this indication.
choice_analysis.C: The current REMS requires a certified prescriber for this use.
choice_analysis.D: State Schedule VI classification and federal REMS requirements operate as different legal layers.
choice_analysis.E: Ordinary state prescription mechanics do not replace the product-specific federal REMS gate.

A REMS restriction is distinct from controlled-substance scheduling.

original_visible_content.stem: A patient asks Pharmacy B to obtain a Massachusetts warfarin prescription from Pharmacy A. The prescription was issued 10 months ago and has three authorized refills remaining. Pharmacy B has a certified pharmacy technician available, and the pharmacist on duty approves the technician’s participation. Which statements are consistent with the current Massachusetts transfer framework? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacies should act on the patient’s transfer request in a timely manner rather than impose a blanket no-transfer rule.

A Schedule VI prescription may be transferred in the same manner as Schedule III-V prescriptions, and the remaining authorized refills may be transferred while the prescription is within the one-year limit.
A certified pharmacy technician may perform a Schedule VI prescription transfer when the pharmacist on duty approves the activity.
Massachusetts requires the transferring pharmacy to charge the patient a transfer fee before releasing the prescription.
The transfer is barred solely because the prescription is more than six months old, even though it was issued less than one year ago.

explanation.core_reasoning: Current 247 CMR 9.14 requires timely transfer at the patient’s request, permits Schedule VI transfers using the Schedule III-V transfer framework, allows transfer of remaining refills, bars Schedule VI transfers after one year from issuance, and prohibits a transfer fee. Separately, 247 CMR 8.04 permits a certified pharmacy technician to perform Schedule VI transfers with pharmacist-on-duty approval.

choice_analysis.A: The current rule affirmatively requires a timely response to the patient or agent’s transfer request.
choice_analysis.B: At 10 months, the Schedule VI prescription remains inside the one-year transfer window and can carry its remaining authorized refills through the transfer pathway.
choice_analysis.C: The certified-technician provision is specific to Schedule VI and depends on pharmacist-on-duty approval.
choice_analysis.D: The Massachusetts rule states that a pharmacy shall not charge a prescription-transfer fee.
choice_analysis.E: The six-month concept should not be imported into the current one-year Schedule VI transfer limit.

related_facts: Warfarin is a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription drug because it is not federally scheduled.
Federal controlled-substance transfer rules should not be overgeneralized into a pharmacist-only rule for Massachusetts Schedule VI transfers.
explanation.mpje_trap: Identify both the prescription’s schedule and the worker’s credential before deciding who may perform the transfer and whether the prescription is still transferable.

explanation.mpje_trap: Either excluding gabapentin because it is Schedule VI or including every Schedule VI drug.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy submits naloxone dispensing information with its daily PMP data. How should the pharmacist understand that submission?

choices.text: It is collected for naloxone reporting purposes but does not appear on the patient's MassPAT profile.
Naloxone becomes federal Schedule II once it is submitted to the PMP.
The submission proves that all naloxone products require a prescription.
Naloxone must appear on the patient profile before the pharmacy may dispense another dose.
PMP submission is prohibited because opioid antagonists may never be reported.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts collects naloxone dispensing data through the PMP mechanism, but those data do not appear on the patient's MassPAT profile.

choice_analysis.A: Current guidance separates data collection from profile display.
choice_analysis.B: Reporting does not change schedule.
choice_analysis.C: OTC and prescription naloxone are distinct products.
choice_analysis.D: The data are not displayed that way.
choice_analysis.E: Massachusetts specifically requests naloxone dispensing data.

related_facts: Patient ID collection is not required for naloxone dispensing data under current guidance.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming every item submitted to the PMP is displayed as controlled-prescription history.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts practitioner with an appropriate MCSR but no DEA registration writes for gabapentin. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The practitioner still needs the appropriate Massachusetts controlled-substance registration authority
A pharmacy dispensing gabapentin generally submits the dispensing data to the Massachusetts PMP
PMP reporting automatically converts gabapentin to federal Schedule V
The pharmacy must use the federal Schedule III/IV five-refills-in-six-months rule solely because gabapentin is reportable
The lack of a DEA registration does not by itself bar Schedule VI-only prescribing of gabapentin

explanation.core_reasoning: Gabapentin combines Massachusetts Schedule VI/MCSR requirements with PMP reporting while remaining outside federal Schedules II-V.

choice_analysis.A: Schedule VI remains controlled under Massachusetts law.
choice_analysis.B: Gabapentin is a designated reportable drug of concern.
choice_analysis.C: Reporting status does not change federal schedule.
choice_analysis.D: PMP status does not import that federal refill rule.
choice_analysis.E: Gabapentin is not federally scheduled.

related_facts: This mixed status is a common Massachusetts-specific exam trap.
explanation.mpje_trap: Letting one regulatory consequence imply every other controlled-substance consequence.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts certified pharmacy technician asks whether he may handle prescription transfers to another pharmacy. The pharmacist on duty is willing to approve. Which transfers may he perform?

choices.text: Transfers of any prescription, because the pharmacist has approved.
Transfers of Schedules III through VI only.
Transfers of Schedule VI controlled substances only.
No transfers, because transfers always require a pharmacist.
Transfers of any non-controlled prescription and Schedule V.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.04(4)(d) permits a certified pharmacy technician, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty, to perform prescription transfers between pharmacies for controlled substances in Schedule VI only, in accordance with 247 CMR 9.00. Pharmacist approval is necessary but does not widen the schedule boundary.

choice_analysis.A: Pharmacist approval does not extend the authority beyond Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.B: The authority does not reach Schedules III through V.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule VI only, with the pharmacist's approval.
choice_analysis.D: A limited transfer authority does exist for certified pharmacy technicians.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule V is outside the stated authority.

related_facts: A plain pharmacy technician has no prescription transfer authority.
explanation.mpje_trap: Pharmacist approval is a precondition to a narrow authority, not a way to expand it.

original_visible_content.stem: A newly hired Massachusetts pharmacist dispenses medications reported to the Prescription Monitoring Program. Her pharmacy holds an institutional MassPAT account that the Manager of Record administers. What does the regulation require of her personally?

choices.text: She shall register with and maintain login information for the monitoring system.
Nothing further, because the pharmacy's account covers all dispensing staff.
She must register only if she dispenses Schedule II controlled substances.
She must register within 30 days of her first Board disciplinary contact.
She must register only if the Manager of Record delegates monitoring duties to her.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.15(1) requires a pharmacist who dispenses medications reported to the Massachusetts Prescription Monitoring Program to register with, and maintain login information for, the electronic system authorized by M.G.L. c. 94C, § 24A, known as PMP or MassPAT. The duty is personal and includes maintaining the login, not merely enrolling once.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: personal registration and maintained login information.
choice_analysis.B: A pharmacy-level account does not discharge the individual duty.
choice_analysis.C: The trigger is dispensing medications reported to the program, not a single schedule.
choice_analysis.D: The duty is not linked to disciplinary contact.
choice_analysis.E: The duty does not depend on delegation by the Manager of Record.

related_facts: The pharmacist must separately make the four validity determinations before filling.
explanation.mpje_trap: An institutional account does not satisfy a duty the regulation places on the dispensing pharmacist.

original_visible_content.stem: A closing Massachusetts pharmacy will move its Schedule II through VI stock to a sister pharmacy. The Manager of Record has given the Board written certified-mail notice with all required particulars and the transfer is set for day 15. Which statements about what follows are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The transferor may keep a small residual stock to finish outstanding prescriptions.
An attestation confirming the inventory is filed with the Board within 30 days.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
Only the transferee's Manager of Record needs to sign the inventory report.
The transferor may possess no controlled substances after the transfer date.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.14(2) requires the transferor to take a complete inventory on the transfer date of all Schedule II through V substances and all Schedule VI substances reportable to the prescription monitoring program, requires BOTH Managers of Record to sign it, requires an attestation with the Board WITHIN TEN DAYS, and provides that the transferor pharmacy may not possess any controlled substances after the transfer date.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation forecloses any possession after the transfer date.
choice_analysis.B: The attestation window is ten days, not thirty.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: reportable Schedule VI is inside the inventory.
choice_analysis.D: Both Managers of Record sign, subject to the unavailability substitution.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: a flat prohibition after the transfer date.

related_facts: A staff pharmacist may sign where the transferor Manager of Record is unavailable
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates carry the 14-day figure forward and use it for the attestation as well.

original_visible_content.stem: An agent collecting a Schedule IV prescription for a housebound Massachusetts patient has no government identification with her. The pharmacist believes refusing would cause the patient real hardship. Which statements about dispensing without a Customer Identifier are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist's belief about hardship is by itself sufficient.
The reason for dispensing without an identifier must be documented.
A regular patient known to the pharmacy is outside the requirement.
The agent must print her name and address and sign for the dispensing.
The requirement reaches Schedule VI dispensings on the same terms.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14)(c) permits dispensing without a Customer Identifier only where the licensee has reason to believe refusal would cause SERIOUS HARDSHIP AND DOCUMENTS THE REASON, AND the ultimate user or agent PRINTS name and address on the reverse of the prescription or in a prescription log AND SIGNS. The requirement itself reaches Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI generally.

choice_analysis.A: The belief is one of three cumulative conditions.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the reason must be documented.
choice_analysis.C: Familiarity is not an exception the regulation recognises.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: printed name and address plus signature.
choice_analysis.E: The requirement is drawn on Schedules II through V and additional drugs.

related_facts: The Commissioner may waive the requirement for refills or deliveries
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates stop at the hardship belief and dispense without the documentation and signature that go with it.

original_visible_content.stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to obtain a prescription issued 13 months ago for a prescription-only drug that is not listed in Schedules I through V. The prescription record shows two authorized refills remaining. Which statements should the receiving pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The remaining refills keep the prescription transferable until both have been dispensed.
The drug falls within Massachusetts Schedule VI because it is a prescription drug not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V.
The transfer must be declined because a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance.
The transfer may proceed, but the receiving pharmacy must apply the federal six-month refill period for Schedule III through V prescriptions.
The rule allowing Schedule VI prescriptions to transfer in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions does not displace the separate one-year transfer ceiling.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts Schedule VI includes prescription drugs not otherwise placed in Schedules I through V. Although 247 CMR 9.14 directs Schedule VI prescriptions to be transferred in the same manner as Schedule III through V prescriptions, it separately provides that a Schedule VI prescription may not be transferred more than one year after issuance. Authorized refills do not extend that age ceiling, and the drug's Massachusetts Schedule VI status does not turn it into a federally controlled Schedule III through V drug.

choice_analysis.A: Authorized refills are relevant only while the prescription remains eligible for transfer; they do not override the one-year ceiling.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the facts place this prescription-only drug in Massachusetts Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: at 13 months, the transfer is outside the permitted one-year period.
choice_analysis.D: The Schedule III through V transfer mechanics do not make this Schedule VI drug federally controlled or substitute a federal refill period for the Massachusetts ceiling.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the general transfer-mechanics direction and the one-year Schedule VI limitation must be read together.

related_facts: A certified pharmacy technician may perform a Schedule VI transfer with approval of the pharmacist on duty
A Massachusetts pharmacy may not charge a fee for transferring a prescription
explanation.mpje_trap: The prescription has refills and follows Schedule III through V transfer mechanics, but neither fact erases the Schedule VI-specific one-year age limit.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is revising the pickup procedure. One prescription is for an ordinary Schedule VI drug that has not been designated by the Commissioner for the additional-drug identification requirement. Another is for a drug that has received that formal designation. Which statements correctly describe the Customer Identifier rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The designated additional drug is within the Customer Identifier rule even though it is not described as a Schedule II through V drug.
Every Schedule VI dispensing is within the rule because Massachusetts calls Schedule VI a controlled-substance schedule.
Dispensing a controlled substance in Schedule II, III, IV, or V is within the rule's stated scope.
The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(14) applies the Customer Identifier requirement when a licensee dispenses a controlled substance in Schedules II through V or an additional drug formally designated under the cited Department regulation. It does not automatically cover every Massachusetts Schedule VI drug. A designated additional drug is covered by the designation, while an ordinary, undesignated Schedule VI drug is not covered merely because Massachusetts places prescription drugs in Schedule VI. Familiarity with the customer is not an independent exception.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: formal additional-drug designation is an independent route into the rule's scope.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation enumerates Schedules II through V and designated additional drugs, not Schedule VI as a whole.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: Schedule II through V dispensing is expressly within the rule.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: Schedule VI classification alone does not satisfy either enumerated route.
choice_analysis.E: Familiarity does not replace identification or, when serious hardship exists, the complete documentation, printed-information, and signature procedure.

related_facts: The Customer Identifier is obtained by inspecting valid government-issued identification of the ultimate user or agent
A serious-hardship dispensing requires both pharmacy documentation and recipient-entered identifying information and signature
explanation.mpje_trap: Massachusetts uses the term Schedule VI broadly, but this identification rule deliberately names Schedules II through V and a separate designation pathway.

original_visible_content.stem:
Case A: A certified technician is asked, with pharmacist approval, to transfer remaining authorized refills of a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription.

Case B: The same employee is asked to transfer a Schedule IV refill between two independent pharmacies and assumes the Schedule VI personnel rule also applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: A certified technician may substitute for the pharmacists in every federal III–V refill transfer.
A technician-performed VI transfer creates a fresh year of validity.
The specified certified-technician transfer authority is for Schedule VI prescriptions.
An urgent patient request converts an ordinary technician into an authorized transfer pharmacist.

explanation.core_reasoning: CPhT의 VI transfer 허용을 II–V로 확대하지 않는다. 연방 III–V refill transfer의 pharmacist-to-pharmacist 조건은 별개다. 담당자의 transfer 권한이 원 처방의 유효기간·잔량을 새로 만들지 않는다. 환자 요청의 urgency가 면허 업무범위를 변경하지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 연방 III–V refill transfer의 pharmacist-to-pharmacist 조건은 별개다.
교정된 설명: The federal controlled-refill transfer requires the licensed-pharmacist communication pathway.
choice_analysis.B:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 담당자의 transfer 권한이 원 처방의 유효기간·잔량을 새로 만들지 않는다.
교정된 설명: Remaining authorization and prescription validity still constrain a permitted VI transfer.
choice_analysis.C: 선택해야 하는 옳은 설명. CPhT의 VI transfer 허용을 II–V로 확대하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.D:
선택하지 않아야 하는 잘못된 설명. 환자 요청의 urgency가 면허 업무범위를 변경하지 않는다.
교정된 설명: The patient's timely-transfer right does not expand the worker's professional scope.

explanation.learning_boundary: 같은 family의 네 문항은 같은 두 사례와 네 판단을 공유하는 연습 변형이다. 독립적인 네 임상 사례로 세지 않는다.

Case B: A separate never-filled Schedule VI prescription originated on paper, and staff assume the controlled EPCS format restriction prohibits its Massachusetts transfer too.

Authority to transfer Schedule VI necessarily includes authority to transfer Schedule III.
Scanning does not qualify the first prescription as an originally electronic prescription for that pathway.
A Schedule VI transfer revives an expired order regardless of authorization.

Include the federally scheduled products but omit gabapentin as nonfederal.
Count the federally scheduled stock and the PMP-reportable gabapentin.
Include oxycodone and clonazepam but omit lower schedules.

explanation.core_reasoning: 평소 재고대장 대상과 MOR 인계 재고 대상은 동일하지 않을 수 있다.

choice_analysis.A: Routine perpetual CII 관리 범위를 change inventory 전체로 잘못 옮긴다.
choice_analysis.B: MA의 사건별 inventory에는 해당 PMP-reportable VI가 들어간다.
choice_analysis.C: MOR change는 CII만이 아니라 II–V와 PMP-reportable VI를 포함한다.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule V와 해당 Schedule VI를 제외할 근거가 없다.

A successful upload automatically documents every pharmacist's clinical query.
Any employee with reporting access may inspect any patient's history for personal interest.
Data submission and patient-specific clinical review are different functions.

Move pregabalin to Schedule VI because both drugs treat neurologic conditions.
Distinguish federal scheduling from gabapentin's state reporting status.
Apply CII no-refill rules to both because their dispensing is reported.

explanation.core_reasoning: Schedule, pharmacologic class, reporting inclusion는 별개 축이다.

choice_analysis.A: PMP 대상에는 해당 Additional Drug가 포함될 수 있다.
choice_analysis.B: 치료계열 유사성이 법적 schedule을 바꾸지 않는다.
choice_analysis.C: Gabapentin은 MA VI·Additional Drug, pregabalin은 federal V라는 구별을 유지한다.
choice_analysis.D: 보고 대상 여부를 CII 분류로 바꾸는 오류이다.

original_visible_content.stem:
A certified technician routinely performs pharmacist-approved Schedule VI prescription transfers. A pharmacist at another pharmacy now calls for the remaining refills of a previously filled Schedule IV prescription. The pharmacies do not share a real-time database, and the prescription is otherwise eligible for its first refill transfer.

How should the pharmacy handle this transfer call? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Let the technician complete the call and have the pharmacist sign the transfer record afterward.
Let the technician transfer the refills because the original prescription has already been dispensed.
Let the technician transfer it after confirming active DEA registrations for both pharmacies.
Connect the receiving pharmacist with the pharmacist on duty to complete the transfer.

explanation.core_reasoning: Transfer가 가능한 처방인지와 누가 transfer communication을 수행할 수 있는지는 별도 판단이다. 첫 refill transfer가 허용되는 CIV라도 CPhT의 CVI 이전 권한으로 처리할 수 없다.

choice_analysis.A: 21 CFR 1306.25(b)(1)은 transfer communication이 두 licensed pharmacists 사이에서 직접 이루어져야 한다고 정한다. Technician이 완료한 통화에 약사가 나중에 서명하는 방식은 직접 약사 간 전달 요건을 충족하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: 이전 조제가 있었다는 사실은 initial unfilled EPCS가 아니라 refill transfer 경로임을 구분한다. 그 경로에도 §1306.25(b)(1)의 약사 간 직접 전달 요건이 남으므로, 이미 조제된 처방이라는 이유로 CPhT에게 CIV 이전 권한이 생기지 않는다.
choice_analysis.C: 약국의 DEA 등록 확인과 직원의 개인 업무범위는 다른 요건이다. CPhT의 주 규정상 transfer 허용은 Schedule VI에 한정되며, 적격 약국 사이의 CIV refill transfer도 약사끼리 직접 전달해야 한다.
choice_analysis.D: 이 사례는 별개 약국 사이의 적격 CIV refill transfer이므로 §1306.25의 직접 pharmacist-to-pharmacist 경로를 사용한다. CPhT가 이전에 수행한 CVI transfer의 허용을 CIV로 옮겨 적용하지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 기존 대표 문항을 별도 사례로 다시 작성했습니다. 원본과 새 문항의 풀이 기록은 각각 보존됩니다. 작성자 출처 대조와 편집 검토이며 독립 법규 감사 또는 실제 시험 난도 보정은 아닙니다.

original_visible_content.stem:
A resident pharmacy's outgoing MOR is seriously ill and unavailable. The proposed new MOR and an authorized staff pharmacist have completed a handover inventory covering Schedules II–V and PMP-reportable Schedule VI stock. The proposed new MOR has signed the inventory report. The owner is not a pharmacist. The pharmacy is preparing the change application and inventory documentation.

Which steps are appropriate for this submission and the associated records? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Let the nonpharmacist owner's application signature replace the unavailable MOR's signature on the inventory report.
Obtain the authorized licensee representative's and proposed new MOR's signatures on the change application.
Use an authorized staff pharmacist's inventory signature and notify the Board why the outgoing MOR cannot sign.
Submit the completed inventory report instead of the change application, retaining the proposed MOR appointment on file.
Retain the completed inventory report with the pharmacy's controlled-substance records after the application is submitted.

explanation.core_reasoning: 신청서와 inventory report는 서명자·목적이 다르다. 중병으로 outgoing MOR가 불가능하면 규정의 authorized staff-pharmacist 경로와 Board 사유 통지를 적용하되, licensee/new-MOR 신청 서명과 실제 inventory 기록 보관도 유지한다.

choice_analysis.A: Licensee 또는 authorized representative가 신청서에 서명하는 권한과 outgoing MOR를 대신하여 inventory report에 서명하는 권한은 별개다. 6.10(2)(a)의 예외는 staff pharmacist를 대상으로 하므로, 비약사 소유자의 신청서 서명이 그 역할을 대체하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: 변경 신청서는 licensee 또는 적법한 authorized representative와 proposed new MOR가 서명한다. Outgoing MOR의 중병은 이 신청서 서명 조합을 비약사 소유자의 단독 서명으로 바꾸는 사유가 아니다.
choice_analysis.C: 중병은 규정이 명시한 outgoing MOR 부재 사유이다. Staff pharmacist가 inventory report의 대체 서명을 하도록 승인되는 경로를 사용할 수 있으며, application 제출 시 그 staff pharmacist가 서명하는 이유를 Board에 알려야 한다. 단순 편의에 따른 대체 서명과는 다르다.
choice_analysis.D: Inventory는 변경 application의 한 구성요소이며, inventory report만으로 Board approval을 위한 change-of-MOR 신청을 대체할 수 없다. 신청서, attestation, 원래 Drug Store Pharmacy license 및 해당 수수료 등의 요구사항은 구분하여 충족한다.
choice_analysis.E: 6.10(2)(a)는 inventory report를 pharmacy의 controlled-substance records에 보관했다는 내용을 attestation에 포함하도록 한다. Application을 제출했다는 이유로 실제 inventory report의 약국 보관이 없어지지 않는다.

explanation.learning_boundary: 기존 대표 문항을 별도 사례로 다시 작성했습니다. 원본과 새 문항의 풀이 기록은 각각 보존됩니다. 작성자 출처 대조와 편집 검토이며 독립 법규 감사 또는 실제 시험 난도 보정은 아닙니다.

original_visible_content.stem:
Two licensed Massachusetts resident pharmacies arrange a closure-related stock transfer under 247 CMR 6.14. The required advance notice has been completed. On the transfer date, the transferor completes the required inventory of Schedules II-V and PMP-reportable Schedule VI drugs. Its manager proposes keeping a small quantity of non-PMP-reportable Schedule VI stock at the transferor pharmacy until a second pickup the following week, because those bottles were not required in that inventory report.

Which assessment correctly addresses the proposed retained stock? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: It may remain because non-PMP-reportable Schedule VI drugs fall outside the specified inventory report.
It may remain for ten days because the inventory attestation is not due until after the transfer.
It may remain if the transferee keeps a copy of the completed transfer inventory for two years.
It may not remain after the transfer date; the possession prohibition also covers those Schedule VI drugs.

explanation.core_reasoning: 같은 조문 안에서도 inventory에 적을 약물 범위와 transferor가 이후 보유하면 안 되는 약물 범위는 다르다. II–V/PMP VI inventory라는 문구를 any controlled substances의 사후 보유금지 예외로 바꾸지 않는다.

choice_analysis.A: 6.14(2)(a)의 transfer-date inventory 대상과 (f)의 transfer 후 보유금지 대상을 혼동했다. Inventory는 II–V와 PMP-reportable VI를 명시하지만 transferor의 사후 보유금지는 any controlled substances이므로 non-PMP VI를 자동 제외하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: 양쪽 pharmacy의 inventory attestation을 transfer 후10일 이내 제출하는 기한은 stock 보유의 유예기간이 아니다. (f)의 기준은 transfer date 이후이며 문서 제출기한까지 보관을 연장하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.C: Inventory report의 양쪽2년 보존과 transferee의 수령·기록유지는 별도 의무다. Receiving pharmacy가 기록을 잘 보관해도 transferor의 controlled-substance possession이 허용되는 것은 아니다.
choice_analysis.D: 이 절차에서 transferor pharmacy는 transfer date 이후 어떤 controlled substances도 보유할 수 없다. 지문이 지정한 non-PMP Schedule VI도 여기에 들어가므로, 재고표에 포함되지 않았다는 이유로 다음 주까지 남겨둘 수 없다. 일상적인 소량 pharmacy-to-pharmacy distribution 전체에 이 closure 규칙을 일반화하지 않는다.
